messages.subject: Re: RODBC Firebird connection
messages.body_plain:
I see a few problems:

1) You appear to be specifying your server's address as "10.42.3.4" which is in the private address space <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_network> and would not be accessible from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers. You need to specify a public IP address or host name.
2) It isn't clear to me that FreeTDS supports <http://www.freetds.org/> Firebird, just MS SQL Server and Sybase

There is an actual Firebird ODBC driver, but it is not available in the Ubuntu <https://help.ubuntu.com/community/ODBC> repositories, and is not currently installed in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

I'll speak with the team and see if it makes sense to add, but at this moment I would say that it is not supported.

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] restrict shinyapps.io geographically?
messages.body_plain:
John,

We don't current support any features to restrict users by geography.

That said, within your shiny application code you might be able to use session$request$REMOTE_ADDR to get the client's IP address and then make a call to a GeoIP <https://freegeoip.net/> service to map that IP address to a country and then choose not to display the application if its outside your targeted geographies. However, because this must be done in your application code, active hours will still be counted. But presumably people would not stick around for very long if they can't interact with the application, so you might see a reduction in active hours.

Please note however this approach will require some testing on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, because I am not sure we're currently exposing the actual client's IP address in session$request$REMOTE_ADDR. If thats the case, it might be a fair bit of work to fix things on our side, and I can't make any guarantees when that would be completed.

If this all sounds a bit complicated and vague, I apologize. I wish I had a better answer for you.

-Andy

My understanding, which is consistent with what happens when I run the app on locally, is that API calls are made when the app starts, but not in response to user input.

Does the entire app, along with the API call, run only once when the application starts? Does it restart for each instance / worker / connection? Generally, what is the appropriate coding practice for what I'm trying to do?

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I recommend starting by reading the shiny docs on scoping <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html> rules which goes into a bit of detail on what the shinyServer() function does. I would also read the performance tuning guide <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scaling-and-tuning.html> since it also explains some of this.

That said, to make things easy to understand its best to remember that under the hood shiny is running inside an R process called a worker. Your server.R file is sourced when that worker is started. These workers in turn can handle multiple sessions. A session (sometimes called a connection) is created when someone connects to the shiny app via a web browser. Each time a session is created, the shinyServer function is run and is scoped to that session.

That said, its impossible to directly answer your question because there are many parameters that you can tune to change how all these things work, which outlined in the performance tuning guide I linked to above. But I believe by default we allow 50 connections per worker, and a maximum of 3 workers.

Hope that helps,
-Andy

messages.body_plain:
I would echo Andy's comments that it is best to read the docs/links that he sent.  That being said, I have included some answers below in case they are helpful.

The code outside shinyServer() will be executed when the R process first starts (in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> this is a Worker).  It does not get re-run for every session, but by definition will happen for every worker, and every instance (since an instance will start at least one Worker).
You would want the logic to check to see when the code was last run, and only run again if 15 minutes have passed.  That being said, I suspect that getting all the appropriate locks in place to make sure you aren't running the same refresh code from more than one R process is going to be error prone.  Instead, I would recommend that your application refreshes the loading of the data that you are likely computing every 15 minutes through a reactivePoll mechanism on a per R worker process basis, and you have an out of band process that refreshes the data.  Maybe look to store the data in an S3 bucket, a dropbox location or a database that is accessible by the R process.  This is a use case that I think we could provide a better model for and is on our list of things that would be nice to add in the coming year if more people are facing it nowadays.

Unfortunately shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> doesn't have a mechanism for scheduling execution of work.  It is one of those ideas we have been considering but hadn't seen enough demand for. You are the second person to bring it up in the past 24 hours so perhaps the idea is gaining more momentum now. Once we add support for persistent storage, and scheduling it will be a much simpler process to do what you want to do.

-Tareef
